title: Azulene Labs Raises $3.4 Million Pre-Seed Round to Build Physics-Grounded AI Foundation Models for Chemistry - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Azulene Labs Raises $3.4 Million Pre-Seed Round to Build Physics-Grounded AI Foundation Models for Chemistry

Molecular simulation developer Azulene Labs has secured a $3.4 million pre-seed financing round to accelerate the development of physics-based AI foundation models designed to replace trial-and-error chemical discovery with predictive computational engineering. Led by quantum-focused venture capital firm Ground State Ventures ($88 million fund), the oversubscribed round includes participation from early investor Entrada Ventures and angel investors.

Headquartered in Berkeley, California, Azulene Labs was founded by CEO Dr. Nicolas Sawaya—a Harvard PhD in chemical physics who previously led quantum algorithm development for chemistry at Intel Labs. The company addresses a fundamental limitation in computational biochemistry: traditional computer models routinely miss ligand-protein binding affinity predictions by factors of a hundred or more, while modern unconstrained AI generative models frequently output physically impossible molecular structures. Azulene Labs rebuilds the simulation stack by training machine learning architectures directly on quantum-mechanical training data, constraining models to underlying physical laws.

The platform delivers roughly 100× the computational efficiency of competing simulation tools while reducing training data generation costs by more than 200×. By introducing engineering-grade predictive precision to molecular design, Azulene Labs targets high-value applications across biopharma (e.g., targeting previously undruggable proteins, novel antibiotics), agriculture, energy storage, industrial chemical solvents, and biodegradable plastics. The team includes founding scientists from Caltech, Harvard, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and MIPT.
